thread:
sam (customer): Hey team — since this morning our Dedicated pool for acct-42 started seeing intermittent 429s and big tail latency spikes when customers do short bursty jobs. Auth errors look fine, no token failures. Can't reproduce consistently though, spikes seem correlated with sudden 3-4x qps bursts.

maria (support): Sorry you're hitting this. Do you have a short repro script or a recent request id we can search for? Also which model/version and pool id?

sam (customer): Pool id is rp-us-east-7, model redwood/4x-large:v3. Example request id: req_20260317_88f. Latency for that req shows 1.2s to first byte then a bunch of 429s right after. We run a bunch of short streamed requests (50–200 tokens) at bursty intervals.

devin (infra): Quick hypothesis: reserved_pool headroom/penalty window is kicking in during quick bursts. Can you share the pattern (QPS timeline) or a simple ab-style script? If you can run this locally, try:

```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.02
done
```

That mimics many short parallel requests.

jasper (oncall): Also check the customer's tokenbucket metrics: reserved_pool.tokens, refill_rate, penalty_window_remaining. We recently adjusted the refill policy for some pools to prioritize steady qps over spikes — that can surface as 429s for bursty traffic.

maria (support): Sam — can you run that script for 30s and paste the timeline (qps per second) and attach any request ids? We can correlate with ingress and pool metrics.

sam (customer): Running now, got a handful of 429s within the first 10s. Request ids: req_20260317_90a, req_20260317_90b, req_20260317_90c. Also noticed billing meter shows a drop for those windows (looks like blocked requests not billed).

devin (infra): Good data — that pattern fits token-bucket exhaustion. Short-term mitigation: enable temporary burst allowance for that pool (increase burst_window from 5s to 15s) or raise reserved_pool.refill_rate by 30%. Long-term: smooth client's traffic with a local leaky-bucket or use client-side pacing to avoid refill starvation.

jasper (oncall): To change pool config:

PATCH /admin/pools/rp-us-east-7
{ "burst_window": 15, "burst_headroom": 1.5 }

Ops will need to approve for SLA-impacting changes. I can file a change with infra now.

maria (support): Also worth checking model switching fallback: if you have a compatible smaller variant (redwood/4x-large:v3-quant), routing to that during peak can avoid capacity throttles. We can help add a canary route.

ops-bot: [automation] Created change request CHG-3741 to increase burst_window on rp-us-east-7 pending infra approval. Link: https://infra.redwood/chg/CHG-3741

devin (infra): For diagnostics, we need these metrics around the timestamps: pool.token_count, pool.refill_rate, pool.penalty_window_active, ingress.backend_latency_ms, auth.latency_ms. If you can't share metrics, we can pull them from our monitoring if you grant support-read perms.

sam (customer): I gave support-read to maria. Also curious — why is billing meter dropping for blocked requests? Is that expected?

maria (support): Blocked (429) requests are not billed as successful tokens, but we log them for incident economics. If you'd like us to allow billing for attempted bursts temporarily, that's a contract change — we can bring this up with account team.

jasper (oncall): Short checklist for triage: 1) capture repro script and request ids (done) 2) pull pool token metrics (in progress) 3) try temporary burst_window bump (CHG-3741) 4) recommend client-side pacing or route to compatible variant 5) follow up on billing policy if needed.

maria (support): I'll coordinate with infra to get CHG-3741 approved and monitor the pool after the change. I'll post back when we see difference. :thumbsup:

sam (customer): Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll add a small client-side queue for now and send additional logs if we still see 429s.

maria (support): Closing loop: infra approved and deployed CHG-3741 at 3061234585. We saw token_count replenish faster and 429s dropped to near zero for 2 minutes of the same synthetic test. Leaving open to monitor for 24h and will convert to permanent config if stable.

jasper (oncall): Follow-ups: consider autoscaling policy tweaks for Dedicated pools so sustained bursts are handled via short-term provisioned spare capacity rather than token boosts. Logged as RFC-688 for product.

sam (customer): Confirmed — running client workload for 10m, looks stable. Thanks everyone. :tada:
